steps.observation: You have 300 seconds. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
1. Expand and electrify public transportation  
   • Build reliable bus-rapid transit and rail networks so residents can forgo private cars.  
   • Power fleets with renewable electricity (battery-electric buses, light-rail, e-taxis), cutting tail-pipe CO₂.  

2. Tighten building-energy standards  
   • Adopt “net-zero” or “passive house” codes for new construction and deep-retrofit programs for existing stock.  
   • Incentivize high-efficiency HVAC, insulation, LED lighting and onsite solar or district heating, lowering heating-cooling emissions—the largest urban source after transport.  

3. Promote compact, mixed-use urban planning  
   • Zone for higher density, mixed residential-commercial areas, and ample cycling-pedestrian infrastructure.  
   • Shorter travel distances reduce vehicle use, while shared walls in multifamily buildings curb per-capita energy demand, jointly driving down citywide carbon footprints.
